He lifted up his eyes, and saw Benjamin, his brother, his mother’s son, and said, “Is this your youngest brother, of whom you spoke to me?” He said, “God be gracious to you, my son.”
Joseph hurried, for his heart yearned over his brother; and he sought a place to weep. He entered into his room, and wept there.
He washed his face, and came out. He controlled himself, and said, “Serve the meal.”
They served him by himself, and them by themselves, and the Egyptians who ate with him by themselves, because the Egyptians don’t eat with the Hebrews, for that is an abomination to the Egyptians.
They sat before him, the firstborn according to his birthright, and the youngest according to his youth, and the men marveled with one another.
He sent portions to them from before him, but Benjamin’s portion was five times as much as any of theirs. They drank, and were merry with him.

44.text: He commanded the steward of his house, saying, “Fill the men’s sacks with food, as much as they can carry, and put each man’s money in his sack’s mouth.
Put my cup, the silver cup, in the sack’s mouth of the youngest, with his grain money.” He did according to the word that Joseph had spoken.
As soon as the morning was light, the men were sent away, they and their donkeys.
When they had gone out of the city, and were not yet far off, Joseph said to his steward, “Up, follow after the men. When you overtake them, ask them, ‘Why have you rewarded evil for good?
Isn’t this that from which my lord drinks, and by which he indeed divines? You have done evil in so doing.’ ”
He overtook them, and he spoke these words to them.
They said to him, “Why does my lord speak such words as these? Far be it from your servants that they should do such a thing!
Behold, the money, which we found in our sacks’ mouths, we brought again to you out of the land of Canaan. How then should we steal silver or gold out of your lord’s house?
With whomever of your servants it is found, let him die, and we also will be my lord’s slaves.”
He said, “Now also let it be according to your words. He with whom it is found will be my slave; and you will be blameless.”
Then they hurried, and each man took his sack down to the ground, and each man opened his sack.
He searched, beginning with the oldest, and ending at the youngest. The cup was found in Benjamin’s sack.
Then they tore their clothes, and each man loaded his donkey, and returned to the city.
Judah and his brothers came to Joseph’s house, and he was still there. They fell on the ground before him.
Joseph said to them, “What deed is this that you have done? Don’t you know that such a man as I can indeed do divination?”

Judah said, “What will we tell my lord? What will we speak? How will we clear ourselves? God has found out the iniquity of your servants. Behold, we are my lord’s slaves, both we and he also in whose hand the cup is found.”
He said, “Far be it from me that I should do so. The man in whose hand the cup is found, he will be my slave; but as for you, go up in peace to your father.”
Then Judah came near to him, and said, “Oh, my lord, please let your servant speak a word in my lord’s ears, and don’t let your anger burn against your servant; for you are even as Pharaoh.
My lord asked his servants, saying, ‘Have you a father, or a brother?’
We said to my lord, ‘We have a father, an old man, and a child of his old age, a little one; and his brother is dead, and he alone is left of his mother; and his father loves him.’
You said to your servants, ‘Bring him down to me, that I may set my eyes on him.’
We said to my lord, ‘The boy can’t leave his father, for if he should leave his father, his father would die.’
You said to your servants, ‘Unless your youngest brother comes down with you, you will see my face no more.’
When we came up to your servant my father, we told him the words of my lord.
Our father said, ‘Go again and buy us a little food.’
We said, ‘We can’t go down. If our youngest brother is with us, then we will go down: for we may not see the man’s face, unless our youngest brother is with us.’
Your servant, my father, said to us, ‘You know that my wife bore me two sons.
One went out from me, and I said, “Surely he is torn in pieces;” and I haven’t seen him since.
If you take this one also from me, and harm happens to him, you will bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to Sheol.’
Now therefore when I come to your servant my father, and the boy is not with us; since his life is bound up in the boy’s life;
it will happen, when he sees that the boy is no more, that he will die. Your servants will bring down the gray hairs of your servant, our father, with sorrow to Sheol.
For your servant became collateral for the boy to my father, saying, ‘If I don’t bring him to you, then I will bear the blame to my father forever.’
Now therefore, please let your servant stay instead of the boy, my lord’s slave; and let the boy go up with his brothers.
For how will I go up to my father, if the boy isn’t with me?—lest I see the evil that will come on my father.”

45.text: Then Joseph couldn’t control himself before all those who stood before him, and he called out, “Cause everyone to go out from me!” No one else stood with him, while Joseph made himself known to his brothers.
He wept aloud. The Egyptians heard, and the house of Pharaoh heard.
Joseph said to his brothers, “I am Joseph! Does my father still live?” His brothers couldn’t answer him; for they were terrified at his presence.
Joseph said to his brothers, “Come near to me, please.” They came near. He said, “I am Joseph, your brother, whom you sold into Egypt.
Now don’t be grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that you sold me here, for God sent me before you to preserve life.
For these two years the famine has been in the land, and there are yet five years, in which there will be no plowing and no harvest.
God sent me before you to preserve for you a remnant on the earth, and to save you alive by a great deliverance.
So now it wasn’t you who sent me here, but God, and he has made me a father to Pharaoh, lord of all his house, and ruler over all the land of Egypt.
Hurry, and go up to my father, and tell him, ‘This is what your son Joseph says, “God has made me lord of all Egypt. Come down to me. Don’t wait.
You shall dwell in the land of Goshen, and you will be near to me, you, your children, your children’s children, your flocks, your herds, and all that you have.
There I will provide for you; for there are yet five years of famine; lest you come to poverty, you, and your household, and all that you have.” ’
Behold, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that it is my mouth that speaks to you.
You shall tell my father of all my glory in Egypt, and of all that you have seen. You shall hurry and bring my father down here.”
He fell on his brother Benjamin’s neck and wept, and Benjamin wept on his neck.
He kissed all his brothers, and wept on them. After that his brothers talked with him.
The report of it was heard in Pharaoh’s house, saying, “Joseph’s brothers have come.” It pleased Pharaoh well, and his servants.
Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Tell your brothers, ‘Do this: Load your animals, and go, travel to the land of Canaan.
Take your father and your households, and come to me, and I will give you the good of the land of Egypt, and you will eat the fat of the land.’
Now you are commanded to do this: Take wagons out of the land of Egypt for your little ones, and for your wives, and bring your father, and come.
Also, don’t concern yourselves about your belongings, for the good of all the land of Egypt is yours.”
The sons of Israel did so. Joseph gave them wagons, according to the commandment of Pharaoh, and gave them provision for the way.
He gave each one of them changes of clothing, but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of clothing.
He sent the following to his father: ten donkeys loaded with the good things of Egypt, and ten female donkeys loaded with grain and bread and provision for his father by the way.
So he sent his brothers away, and they departed. He said to them, “See that you don’t quarrel on the way.”
They went up out of Egypt, and came into the land of Canaan, to Jacob their father.
They told him, saying, “Joseph is still alive, and he is ruler over all the land of Egypt.” His heart fainted, for he didn’t believe them.
They told him all the words of Joseph, which he had said to them. When he saw the wagons which Joseph had sent to carry him, the spirit of Jacob, their father, revived.
Israel said, “It is enough. Joseph my son is still alive. I will go and see him before I die.”

46.text: Israel traveled with all that he had, and came to Beersheba, and offered sacrifices to the God of his father, Isaac.
God spoke to Israel in the visions of the night, and said, “Jacob, Jacob!” He said, “Here I am.”
He said, “I am God, the God of your father. Don’t be afraid to go down into Egypt, for there I will make of you a great nation.
I will go down with you into Egypt. I will also surely bring you up again. Joseph’s hand will close your eyes.”
Jacob rose up from Beersheba, and the sons of Israel carried Jacob, their father, their little ones, and their wives, in the wagons which Pharaoh had sent to carry him.
They took their livestock, and their goods, which they had gotten in the land of Canaan, and came into Egypt—Jacob, and all his offspring with him,
his sons, and his sons’ sons with him, his daughters, and his sons’ daughters, and he brought all his offspring with him into Egypt.
These are the names of the children of Israel, who came into Egypt, Jacob and his sons: Reuben, Jacob’s firstborn.
The sons of Reuben: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
The sons of Simeon: Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul the son of a Canaanite woman.
The sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
The sons of Judah: Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez, and Zerah; but Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan. The sons of Perez were Hezron and Hamul.
The sons of Issachar: Tola, Puvah, Iob, and Shimron.
The sons of Zebulun: Sered, Elon, and Jahleel.
These are the sons of Leah, whom she bore to Jacob in Paddan Aram, with his daughter Dinah. All the souls of his sons and his daughters were thirty-three.
The sons of Gad: Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arodi, and Areli.
The sons of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, Beriah, and Serah their sister. The sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel.
These are the sons of Zilpah, whom Laban gave to Leah, his daughter, and these she bore to Jacob, even sixteen souls.
The sons of Rachel, Jacob’s wife: Joseph and Benjamin.
To Joseph in the land of Egypt were born Manasseh and Ephraim, whom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, bore to him.
The sons of Benjamin: Bela, Becher, Ashbel, Gera, Naaman, Ehi, Rosh, Muppim, Huppim, and Ard.
These are the sons of Rachel, who were born to Jacob: all the souls were fourteen.
The son of Dan: Hushim.
The sons of Naphtali: Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.
These are the sons of Bilhah, whom Laban gave to Rachel, his daughter, and these she bore to Jacob: all the souls were seven.
All the souls who came with Jacob into Egypt, who were his direct offspring, in addition to Jacob’s sons’ wives, all the souls were sixty-six.
The sons of Joseph, who were born to him in Egypt, were two souls. All the souls of the house of Jacob, who came into Egypt, were seventy.
Jacob sent Judah before him to Joseph, to show the way before him to Goshen, and they came into the land of Goshen.
Joseph prepared his chariot, and went up to meet Israel, his father, in Goshen. He presented himself to him, and fell on his neck, and wept on his neck a good while.
Israel said to Joseph, “Now let me die, since I have seen your face, that you are still alive.”
Joseph said to his brothers, and to his father’s house, “I will go up, and speak with Pharaoh, and will tell him, ‘My brothers, and my father’s house, who were in the land of Canaan, have come to me.
These men are shepherds, for they have been keepers of livestock, and they have brought their flocks, and their herds, and all that they have.’
It will happen, when Pharaoh summons you, and will say, ‘What is your occupation?’

that you shall say, ‘Your servants have been keepers of livestock from our youth even until now, both we, and our fathers:’ that you may dwell in the land of Goshen; for every shepherd is an abomination to the Egyptians.”

47.text: Then Joseph went in and told Pharaoh, and said, “My father and my brothers, with their flocks, their herds, and all that they own, have come out of the land of Canaan; and behold, they are in the land of Goshen.”
From among his brothers he took five men, and presented them to Pharaoh.
Pharaoh said to his brothers, “What is your occupation?” They said to Pharaoh, “Your servants are shepherds, both we, and our fathers.”

They also said to Pharaoh, “We have come to live as foreigners in the land, for there is no pasture for your servants’ flocks. For the famine is severe in the land of Canaan. Now therefore, please let your servants dwell in the land of Goshen.”
Pharaoh spoke to Joseph, saying, “Your father and your brothers have come to you.

The land of Egypt is before you. Make your father and your brothers dwell in the best of the land. Let them dwell in the land of Goshen. If you know any able men among them, then put them in charge of my livestock.”
Joseph brought in Jacob, his father, and set him before Pharaoh; and Jacob blessed Pharaoh.
Pharaoh said to Jacob, “How old are you?”

Jacob said to Pharaoh, “The years of my pilgrimage are one hundred thirty years. The days of the years of my life have been few and evil. They have not attained to the days of the years of the life of my fathers in the days of their pilgrimage.”
Jacob blessed Pharaoh, and went out from the presence of Pharaoh.
Joseph placed his father and his brothers, and gave them a possession in the land of Egypt, in the best of the land, in the land of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded.
Joseph provided his father, his brothers, and all of his father’s household with bread, according to the sizes of their families.
There was no bread in all the land; for the famine was very severe, so that the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan fainted by reason of the famine.
Joseph gathered up all the money that was found in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, for the grain which they bought: and Joseph brought the money into Pharaoh’s house.
When the money was all spent in the land of Egypt, and in the land of Canaan, all the Egyptians came to Joseph, and said, “Give us bread, for why should we die in your presence? For our money fails.”
Joseph said, “Give me your livestock; and I will give you food for your livestock, if your money is gone.”

They brought their livestock to Joseph, and Joseph gave them bread in exchange for the horses, and for the flocks, and for the herds, and for the donkeys: and he fed them with bread in exchange for all their livestock for that year.

When that year was ended, they came to him the second year, and said to him, “We will not hide from my lord how our money is all spent, and the herds of livestock are my lord’s. There is nothing left in the sight of my lord, but our bodies, and our lands.

Why should we die before your eyes, both we and our land? Buy us and our land for bread, and we and our land will be servants to Pharaoh. Give us seed, that we may live, and not die, and that the land won’t be desolate.”
So Joseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh, for every man of the Egyptians sold his field, because the famine was severe on them, and the land became Pharaoh’s.
As for the people, he moved them to the cities from one end of the border of Egypt even to the other end of it.
Only he didn’t buy the land of the priests, for the priests had a portion from Pharaoh, and ate their portion which Pharaoh gave them. That is why they didn’t sell their land.
Then Joseph said to the people, “Behold, I have bought you and your land today for Pharaoh. Behold, here is seed for you, and you shall sow the land.

It will happen at the harvests, that you shall give a fifth to Pharaoh, and four parts will be your own, for seed of the field, for your food, for them of your households, and for food for your little ones.”
They said, “You have saved our lives! Let us find favor in the sight of my lord, and we will be Pharaoh’s servants.”
Joseph made it a statute concerning the land of Egypt to this day, that Pharaoh should have the fifth. Only the land of the priests alone didn’t become Pharaoh’s.
Israel lived in the land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen; and they got themselves possessions therein, and were fruitful, and multiplied exceedingly.
Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years. So the days of Jacob, the years of his life, were one hundred forty-seven years.

The time came near that Israel must die, and he called his son Joseph, and said to him, “If now I have found favor in your sight, please put your hand under my thigh, and deal kindly and truly with me. Please don’t bury me in Egypt,
but when I sleep with my fathers, you shall carry me out of Egypt, and bury me in their burying place.” Joseph said, “I will do as you have said.”
Israel said, “Swear to me,” and he swore to him. Then Israel bowed himself on the bed’s head.

48.text: After these things, someone said to Joseph, “Behold, your father is sick.” He took with him his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.
Someone told Jacob, and said, “Behold, your son Joseph comes to you,” and Israel strengthened himself, and sat on the bed.
Jacob said to Joseph, “God Almighty appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan, and blessed me,
and said to me, ‘Behold, I will make you fruitful, and multiply you, and I will make of you a company of peoples, and will give this land to your offspring after you for an everlasting possession.’
Now your two sons, who were born to you in the land of Egypt before I came to you into Egypt, are mine; Ephraim and Manasseh, even as Reuben and Simeon, will be mine.
Your offspring, whom you become the father of after them, will be yours. They will be called after the name of their brothers in their inheritance.

As for me, when I came from Paddan, Rachel died beside me in the land of Canaan on the way, when there was still some distance to come to Ephrath, and I buried her there on the way to Ephrath (also called Bethlehem).”
Israel saw Joseph’s sons, and said, “Who are these?”
Joseph said to his father, “They are my sons, whom God has given me here.” He said, “Please bring them to me, and I will bless them.”
Now the eyes of Israel were dim for age, so that he couldn’t see well. Joseph brought them near to him; and he kissed them, and embraced them.
Israel said to Joseph, “I didn’t think I would see your face, and behold, God has let me see your offspring also.”
Joseph brought them out from between his knees, and he bowed himself with his face to the earth.
Joseph took them both, Ephraim in his right hand toward Israel’s left hand, and Manasseh in his left hand toward Israel’s right hand, and brought them near to him.
Israel stretched out his right hand, and laid it on Ephraim’s head, who was the younger, and his left hand on Manasseh’s head, guiding his hands knowingly, for Manasseh was the firstborn.
He blessed Joseph, and said, “The God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked, the God who has fed me all my life long to this day,
the angel who has redeemed me from all evil, bless the lads, and let my name be named on them, and the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac. Let them grow into a multitude upon the earth.”
When Joseph saw that his father laid his right hand on the head of Ephraim, it displeased him. He held up his father’s hand, to remove it from Ephraim’s head to Manasseh’s head.
Joseph said to his father, “Not so, my father, for this is the firstborn. Put your right hand on his head.”

His father refused, and said, “I know, my son, I know. He also will become a people, and he also will be great. However, his younger brother will be greater than he, and his offspring will become a multitude of nations.”
He blessed them that day, saying, “Israel will bless in your name, saying, ‘God make you as Ephraim and as Manasseh’ ” He set Ephraim before Manasseh.
Israel said to Joseph, “Behold, I am dying, but God will be with you, and bring you again to the land of your fathers.
Moreover I have given to you one portion above your brothers, which I took out of the hand of the Amorite with my sword and with my bow.”

49.text: Jacob called to his sons, and said: “Gather yourselves together, that I may tell you that which will happen to you in the days to come.
Assemble yourselves, and hear, you sons of Jacob. Listen to Israel, your father.
“Reuben, you are my firstborn, my might, and the beginning of my strength, excelling in dignity, and excelling in power.
Boiling over like water, you shall not excel, because you went up to your father’s bed, then defiled it. He went up to my couch.
“Simeon and Levi are brothers. Their swords are weapons of violence.
My soul, don’t come into their council. My glory, don’t be united to their assembly; for in their anger they killed men. In their self-will they hamstrung cattle.
Cursed be their anger, for it was fierce; and their wrath, for it was cruel. I will divide them in Jacob, and scatter them in Israel.
“Judah, your brothers will praise you. Your hand will be on the neck of your enemies. Your father’s sons will bow down before you.
Judah is a lion’s cub. From the prey, my son, you have gone up. He stooped down, he crouched as a lion, as a lioness. Who will rouse him up?
The scepter will not depart from Judah, nor the ruler’s staff from between his feet, until he comes to whom it belongs. The obedience of the peoples will be to him.
Binding his foal to the vine, his donkey’s colt to the choice vine, he has washed his garments in wine, his robes in the blood of grapes.
His eyes will be red with wine, his teeth white with milk.
“Zebulun will dwell at the haven of the sea. He will be for a haven of ships. His border will be on Sidon.
“Issachar is a strong donkey, lying down between the saddlebags.
He saw a resting place, that it was good, the land, that it was pleasant. He bows his shoulder to the burden, and becomes a servant doing forced labor.
“Dan will judge his people, as one of the tribes of Israel.
Dan will be a serpent on the trail, an adder in the path, that bites the horse’s heels, so that his rider falls backward.
I have waited for your salvation, LORD.
“A troop will press on Gad, but he will press on their heel.
“Asher’s food will be rich. He will produce royal dainties.
“Naphtali is a doe set free, who bears beautiful fawns.
“Joseph is a fruitful vine, a fruitful vine by a spring. His branches run over the wall.
The archers have severely grieved him, shot at him, and persecuted him:
But his bow remained strong. The arms of his hands were made strong, by the hands of the Mighty One of Jacob, (from there is the shepherd, the stone of Israel),

even by the God of your father, who will help you, by the Almighty, who will bless you, with blessings of heaven above, blessings of the deep that lies below, blessings of the breasts, and of the womb.

The blessings of your father have prevailed above the blessings of my ancestors, above the boundaries of the ancient hills. They will be on the head of Joseph, on the crown of the head of him who is separated from his brothers.
“Benjamin is a ravenous wolf. In the morning he will devour the prey. At evening he will divide the plunder.”
All these are the twelve tribes of Israel, and this is what their father spoke to them, and blessed them. He blessed everyone according to his own blessing.
He instructed them, and said to them, “I am to be gathered to my people. Bury me with my fathers in the cave that is in the field of Ephron the Hittite,
in the cave that is in the field of Machpelah, which is before Mamre, in the land of Canaan, which Abraham bought with the field from Ephron the Hittite as a burial place.
There they buried Abraham and Sarah, his wife. There they buried Isaac and Rebekah, his wife, and there I buried Leah:
the field and the cave that is therein, which was purchased from the children of Heth.”
When Jacob finished charging his sons, he gathered up his feet into the bed, breathed his last breath, and was gathered to his people.

50.text: Joseph fell on his father’s face, wept on him, and kissed him.
Joseph commanded his servants, the physicians, to embalm his father; and the physicians embalmed Israel.
Forty days were used for him, for that is how many days it takes to embalm. The Egyptians wept for Israel for seventy days.
When the days of weeping for him were past, Joseph spoke to Pharaoh’s staff, saying, “If now I have found favor in your eyes, please speak in the ears of Pharaoh, saying,

‘My father made me swear, saying, “Behold, I am dying. Bury me in my grave which I have dug for myself in the land of Canaan.” Now therefore, please let me go up and bury my father, and I will come again.’ ”
Pharaoh said, “Go up, and bury your father, just like he made you swear.”
Joseph went up to bury his father; and with him went up all the servants of Pharaoh, the elders of his house, all the elders of the land of Egypt,
all the house of Joseph, his brothers, and his father’s house. Only their little ones, their flocks, and their herds, they left in the land of Goshen.
Both chariots and horsemen went up with him. It was a very great company.
They came to the threshing floor of Atad, which is beyond the Jordan, and there they lamented with a very great and severe lamentation. He mourned for his father seven days.

When the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, saw the mourning in the floor of Atad, they said, “This is a grievous mourning by the Egyptians.” Therefore its name was called Abel Mizraim, which is beyond the Jordan.
His sons did to him just as he commanded them,

for his sons carried him into the land of Canaan, and buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah, which Abraham bought with the field, as a possession for a burial site, from Ephron the Hittite, near Mamre.
Joseph returned into Egypt—he, and his brothers, and all that went up with him to bury his father, after he had buried his father.
When Joseph’s brothers saw that their father was dead, they said, “It may be that Joseph will hate us, and will fully pay us back for all the evil which we did to him.”
They sent a message to Joseph, saying, “Your father commanded before he died, saying,

‘You shall tell Joseph, “Now please forgive the disobedience of your brothers, and their sin, because they did evil to you.” ’ Now, please forgive the disobedience of the servants of the God of your father.” Joseph wept when they spoke to him.
His brothers also went and fell down before his face; and they said, “Behold, we are your servants.”
Joseph said to them, “Don’t be afraid, for am I in the place of God?
As for you, you meant evil against me, but God meant it for good, to save many people alive, as is happening today.
Now therefore don’t be afraid. I will provide for you and your little ones.” He comforted them, and spoke kindly to them.
Joseph lived in Egypt, he, and his father’s house. Joseph lived one hundred ten years.
Joseph saw Ephraim’s children to the third generation. The children also of Machir, the son of Manasseh, were born on Joseph’s knees.
Joseph said to his brothers, “I am dying, but God will surely visit you, and bring you up out of this land to the land which he swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.”
Joseph took an oath from the children of Israel, saying, “God will surely visit you, and you shall carry up my bones from here.”
So Joseph died, being one hundred ten years old, and they embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt.

chapters.title: Creation
chapters.summary: In the beginning God creates the heavens and the earth. He speaks, and light, sky, land, and plants appear over three days. Sun, moon, stars, sea animals, and birds follow. On the sixth day he makes land animals and then people. He makes people in his own image, male and female. He blesses them and tells them to fill the earth and rule the animals. He gives plants as food to people and animals. God sees all he has made and calls it very good.
chapters.meaning: Six times the chapter says God saw that his work was good. People come last, and verse 31 says “very good.” Verse 27 says “image” twice and then names both male and female. No one group holds that standing alone. The command to rule in verse 28 comes after the blessing. Verses 29–30 then give plants as food to people and animals alike. So ruling here sits beside care for life that God called good.

God plants a garden in Eden with a river and two named trees. He puts the man there to work it and keep it. He forbids one tree and warns of death. God says it is not good for the man to be alone. The man names the animals, but none is a helper like him. God makes a woman from his rib, and the man welcomes her as his flesh.

The man’s words in verse 23 are about likeness: bone of his bones.

Their eyes open, and they cover themselves and hide. God asks where the man is and whether he ate. The man blames the woman, and the woman blames the serpent. God curses the serpent and the ground, and speaks of pain and hard work. He clothes them with skins and sends them out of Eden.

chapters.summary: Eve bears Cain and then Abel. Cain farms, and Abel keeps sheep. Both bring offerings, and the LORD accepts Abel’s but not Cain’s. The LORD warns Cain that sin crouches at the door. Cain kills Abel in the field and asks if he is his brother’s keeper. The LORD sends Cain away as a wanderer but marks him for protection. Cain’s family builds a city, and Lamech boasts of killing a man. Eve bears Seth, and people begin to call on the LORD’s name.

chapters.summary: This is the family record from Adam to Noah. God made people in his likeness, and Adam fathers Seth in his own likeness. Each entry gives a father’s age, his son, his total years, and his death. The years are very long, up to 969 for Methuselah. Enoch’s entry is different. He walks with God, and God takes him. Lamech names his son Noah and hopes for comfort from the cursed ground. Noah fathers Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
chapters.meaning: The chapter repeats one pattern eight times and ends each with “then he died.” Genesis 2:17 warned of death, and the list shows it arriving. chapters.summary: People multiply, and God’s sons take human daughters as wives. The LORD says man’s days will be 120 years. He sees that human thoughts are evil all the time, and he is grieved. He decides to wipe out people and animals. But Noah finds favor and walks with God. God tells Noah the earth is filled with violence. He orders a ship of gopher wood with three levels and one door. Noah is to bring his family, pairs of animals, and food, and he obeys.

Verse 6 shows the decision costs God grief. Verse 8 keeps one door open: Noah finds favor.

chapters.title: The flood
chapters.summary: The LORD tells Noah to enter the ship with his household. Noah takes seven pairs of clean animals and one pair of the others. Noah is six hundred years old. After seven days the deep bursts open and the sky’s windows open. Rain falls forty days and nights. Noah’s family and the animals go in, and the LORD shuts him in. The water lifts the ship and covers the high mountains. Everything on dry land dies, and only those in the ship remain.
chapters.meaning: Noah builds the ship and loads it, as verses 5 and 9 say. One act is not his: closing the door. Verse 16 says “the LORD shut him in.” Noah’s safety rests on that act, not on his building alone. The closed door keeps the family in and the water out. It also marks the end of the time to enter. Verse 23 states the result: only those inside are left.

The dove comes back with an olive leaf, then does not return. God tells Noah to leave the ship with his family and the animals. Noah builds an altar and offers burnt offerings. The LORD says he will not again curse the ground or strike every living thing. Seedtime and harvest, summer and winter, day and night will not stop.

Each list ends with families, languages, lands, and nations. From these families the nations spread over the earth.

people.name: Noah
people.role: Builder of the ship in the flood
people.relations: Son of Lamech. Father of Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
people.meaning: God tells him to build a ship, and he does all that God commands. He takes his family and the animals inside. After the flood he builds an altar. God makes a covenant never to destroy the earth by flood again.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Shem
people.relations: Brother of Ham and Japheth. Abram comes from his line.
people.meaning: He and Japheth cover their father Noah without looking at him. Noah blesses the LORD, the God of Shem. Genesis 11 follows his line down to Terah and Abram.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Ham
people.relations: Father of Canaan. Brother of Shem and Japheth.
people.meaning: He sees his father Noah uncovered and tells his two brothers. Noah then curses Ham’s son Canaan, not Ham. The passage gives no support for racial slavery.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Japheth
people.relations: Brother of Shem and Ham.
people.meaning: He helps Shem cover their father Noah. Noah asks God to enlarge Japheth. Genesis 10 lists his sons and the peoples that come from them.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Nimrod
people.relations: Son of Cush. Grandson of Ham.
people.meaning: He becomes a mighty one on the earth. People say, “like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before the LORD.” His kingdom begins with Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh in Shinar.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Abraham / Abram
people.role: Man God calls to Canaan and promises a nation
people.relations: Husband of Sarah. Father of Ishmael and Isaac. Uncle of Lot.
people.meaning: God tells him to leave Haran, and he goes to Canaan. Out of fear he twice calls Sarah his sister. God promises him land and a son, and Sarah bears Isaac. He goes to offer Isaac, and the LORD’s angel stops him.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Sarah / Sarai
people.relations: Wife of Abraham. Mistress of Hagar.
people.meaning: She has no child and gives Hagar to Abram. She then treats Hagar harshly. She laughs when she hears she will bear a son. She bears Isaac and tells Abraham to send Hagar and Ishmael away.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Lot
people.relations: Son of Haran. Father of two daughters in Genesis 19.
people.meaning: He parts from Abram and chooses the plain of the Jordan near Sodom. Kings carry him off, and Abram rescues him. Two angels lead him out before Sodom is destroyed. His two daughters later make him drunk and bear his sons.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Hagar
people.role: Egyptian servant and mother of Ishmael
people.relations: Servant of Sarah. Mother of Ishmael, Abraham’s first son.
people.meaning: She conceives by Abram and runs from Sarai’s harsh treatment. The LORD’s angel finds her by a spring. She calls the LORD “a God who sees.” Later Abraham sends her away, and God hears her son’s voice.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Ishmael
people.relations: Half-brother of Isaac. Father of twelve princes.
people.meaning: The LORD’s angel tells Hagar to name him Ishmael. Abraham sends him away with Hagar, and God hears his voice. God promises to make him a great nation. He and Isaac later bury Abraham.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Melchizedek
people.relations: Genesis names no family for him. He meets Abram after Lot’s rescue.
people.meaning: He brings out bread and wine after Abram rescues Lot. He blesses Abram and blesses God Most High. Abram gives him a tenth of all. LDS scripture says more about his work as priest.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Isaac
people.relations: Husband of Rebekah. Father of Esau and Jacob.
people.meaning: God promises him to Abraham and Sarah, and Sarah bears him. Abraham binds him on an altar, and God provides a ram. He marries Rebekah and digs his father’s wells again. When he is old and cannot see, he blesses Jacob in place of Esau.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Rebekah
people.relations: Daughter of Bethuel. Sister of Laban. Wife of Isaac.
people.meaning: She draws water for Abraham’s servant and his camels. She agrees to go to Canaan and marry Isaac. She bears twins, Esau and Jacob, and loves Jacob. She dresses Jacob as Esau so that Isaac blesses him.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Abimelech
people.role: King who deals with Abraham and Isaac
people.relations: He deals with Abraham in Genesis 20–21. An Abimelech deals with Isaac in Genesis 26. Phicol leads his army.
people.meaning: He takes Sarah, and God warns him in a dream. He gives her back and swears an oath with Abraham at Beersheba. In Genesis 26 an Abimelech learns that Rebekah is Isaac’s wife. Genesis does not say if this is the same king.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Esau / Edom
people.relations: Twin brother of Jacob. Ancestor of Edom.
people.meaning: He sells his birthright to Jacob for bread and lentil stew. Jacob then takes his blessing, and Esau plans to kill him. Years later he runs to meet Jacob and kisses him. He settles in the hill country of Seir.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Jacob / Israel
people.relations: Son of Isaac and Rebekah. Father of twelve sons and Dinah.
people.meaning: He buys Esau’s birthright and tricks Isaac to get the blessing. Laban then tricks him, and he works twenty years for Laban. He wrestles a man at night and is named Israel. In old age he goes to Egypt to see Joseph.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Laban
people.relations: Father of Leah and Rachel. Jacob works for him.
people.meaning: He welcomes Abraham’s servant and lets Rebekah go. He gives Jacob Leah in place of Rachel after seven years of work. Jacob says Laban changed his wages ten times. Laban chases Jacob to Gilead, and they make a covenant there.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Leah
people.role: Mother of six sons and Dinah
people.relations: Daughter of Laban. Wife of Jacob. Sister of Rachel.
people.meaning: Laban gives her to Jacob in place of Rachel. Jacob loves Rachel more, and the LORD gives Leah children. She names Reuben for her pain and Judah for her praise. Jacob buries her in the cave of Machpelah.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Rachel
people.relations: Daughter of Laban. Wife of Jacob. Sister of Leah.
people.meaning: Jacob loves her and works fourteen years for her and Leah. She has no child for years, then bears Joseph. She takes her father’s teraphim when the family leaves. She dies giving birth to Benjamin on the way to Ephrath.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Bilhah
people.relations: Rachel’s servant. Mother of two of Jacob’s sons.
people.meaning: Laban gives her to Rachel as a servant. Rachel gives her to Jacob, and she bears Dan and Naphtali. Rachel names both boys. Reuben later lies with her, and Genesis gives her no words.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Zilpah
people.relations: Leah’s servant. Mother of two of Jacob’s sons.
people.meaning: Laban gives her to Leah as a servant. Leah gives her to Jacob, and she bears Gad and Asher. Leah names both boys. Genesis gives Zilpah no words.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Dinah
people.relations: Sister of Simeon and Levi.
people.meaning: She goes out to see the daughters of the land. Shechem, son of Hamor, takes her and lies with her. Simeon and Levi kill the city’s men and take her from Shechem’s house. Genesis gives her no words.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Joseph
people.role: Son sold into Egypt who later rules under Pharaoh
people.relations: Son of Jacob and Rachel. Husband of Asenath. Father of Ephraim and Manasseh.
people.meaning: His brothers hate him and sell him, and he is taken to Egypt. Potiphar’s wife accuses him falsely, and he goes to prison. He explains Pharaoh’s dreams and stores grain for the famine. He feeds his family and tells his brothers God meant it for good.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Judah
people.relations: Son of Jacob and Leah. Father of Perez and Zerah through Tamar.
people.meaning: He tells his brothers to sell Joseph and not kill him. He keeps Tamar from his son Shelah, then says she is more righteous. He promises Jacob to bring Benjamin back. In Egypt he offers to stay as a slave in Benjamin’s place.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Reuben
people.relations: Son of Jacob and Leah. Brother of Joseph.
people.meaning: He lies with Bilhah, and his father hears of it. He tells his brothers not to kill Joseph and plans to bring him home. He offers his two sons as a pledge for Benjamin. Jacob says Reuben will not excel.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Simeon
people.relations: Brother of Levi and Dinah.
people.meaning: He and Levi kill the men of Shechem after Shechem defiles Dinah. Joseph later binds him and keeps him in Egypt. He goes free when the brothers bring Benjamin. Jacob curses the anger of Simeon and Levi.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Levi
people.relations: Brother of Simeon and Dinah.
people.meaning: He and Simeon kill the men of Shechem and take Dinah away. Jacob says they have brought him trouble. In his last words Jacob curses their anger and says he will scatter them.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Benjamin
people.relations: Son of Jacob and Rachel. Full brother of Joseph.
people.meaning: Rachel dies at his birth and names him Benoni, but Jacob names him Benjamin. Jacob fears to send him to Egypt. Joseph’s cup is found in his sack. Judah offers to stay as a slave in his place.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Tamar
people.role: Judah’s daughter-in-law who bears his twin sons
people.relations: Widow of Er and Onan. Mother of Perez and Zerah.
people.meaning: Judah sends her home and does not give her to his son Shelah. She veils herself, and Judah lies with her without knowing her. She keeps his signet, cords, and staff. When Judah sees them he says she is more righteous.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Potiphar
people.relations: Husband of the unnamed woman who accuses Joseph.
people.meaning: He buys Joseph and puts him over his whole house. His wife says Joseph tried to lie with her. He grows angry and puts Joseph in the king’s prison.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Pharaoh
people.relations: The Pharaoh of Genesis 12 deals with Abram and Sarai. A later Pharaoh deals with Joseph and Jacob.
people.meaning: In Genesis 12 a Pharaoh takes Sarai and then sends Abram away. In Joseph’s time a Pharaoh dreams of seven fat and seven thin cattle. He sets Joseph over Egypt and gives Jacob’s family land in Goshen. Genesis names no Pharaoh.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Asenath
people.relations: Daughter of Potiphera, priest of On. Mother of Manasseh and Ephraim.
people.meaning: Pharaoh gives her to Joseph as a wife. She bears Manasseh and Ephraim before the famine. Genesis tells nothing else about her.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Ephraim
people.relations: Son of Joseph and Asenath. Brother of Manasseh.
people.meaning: He is born in Egypt before the famine. Jacob takes him as his own son. Jacob puts his right hand on Ephraim, the younger. Jacob says the younger brother will be greater.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

people.name: Manasseh
people.relations: Son of Joseph and Asenath. Brother of Ephraim.
people.meaning: He is Joseph’s firstborn, born in Egypt. Jacob takes him as his own son. Jacob puts his left hand on Manasseh and his right on Ephraim. Joseph objects, but Jacob says Manasseh will also be great.
people.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.

places.name: Ur
places.summary: Terah’s son Haran dies in Ur of the Chaldees. Terah leaves Ur with Abram, Sarai, and Lot in Genesis 11. Southern Ur is a common choice for the site.
places.limits: Scholars still debate which place Genesis means.

places.name: Haran
places.summary: Terah’s family settles here, and Terah dies (Genesis 11). Abram leaves Haran for Canaan in Genesis 12. Jacob later flees here to Laban.
places.limits: The ancient city is near modern Harran.

places.name: Babel / Babylon
places.summary: Nimrod’s kingdom begins at Babel in Genesis 10. In Genesis 11 people build a city and a tower in Shinar. The LORD confuses their language, and the city is named Babel.
places.limits: Babylon is the usual choice for the city. No one has identified the tower.

places.name: Mountains of Ararat
places.summary: The ship rests on Ararat’s mountains in Genesis 8.
places.limits: The marker shows a broad mountain region, not one peak.

places.name: Shechem
places.summary: Abram builds an altar here in Genesis 12. Jacob buys land here in Genesis 33. In Genesis 34 Simeon and Levi kill the men of the city. Joseph looks for his brothers here in Genesis 37.
places.limits: Tell Balata is the usual ancient city site.

places.name: Bethel
places.summary: Abram builds an altar near Bethel in Genesis 12 and returns in Genesis 13. Jacob dreams here and names the place Bethel (Genesis 28). God sends Jacob back here in Genesis 35.
places.limits: Beitin is a common identification. The exact ancient site is not sure.

places.name: Hebron / Machpelah
places.summary: Abram lives by the oaks of Mamre in Hebron (Genesis 13). Sarah dies here, and Abraham buys the cave of Machpelah (Genesis 23). Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob are later buried in that cave.
places.limits: The marker shows Hebron. It does not prove where the burial cave is.

places.name: Beersheba
places.summary: Abraham and Abimelech swear an oath here in Genesis 21. Isaac makes his own oath with Abimelech in Genesis 26. Jacob offers sacrifices here on his way to Egypt (Genesis 46).
places.limits: The marker shows the area of the ancient town.

places.name: Egypt / Nile valley
places.summary: Abram goes to Egypt in a famine (Genesis 12). Joseph is sold there and rises to rule under Pharaoh. Jacob’s family moves there in Genesis 46.
places.limits: The marker shows the whole region, not one city.

places.name: Goshen / eastern delta
places.summary: Joseph settles Jacob’s family in Goshen in Genesis 46–47. Pharaoh calls it the best of the land.
places.limits: The marker shows a broad part of the delta. Goshen’s exact limits are unknown.

places.name: Sodom / Dead Sea region
places.summary: Lot moves his tent as far as Sodom in Genesis 13. Abraham pleads for the city in Genesis 18. In Genesis 19 the LORD rains sulfur and fire on it.
places.limits: The site is disputed. The marker shows a region, not a known city.

places.name: Zoar / Dead Sea region
places.summary: Lot asks to flee to this small city in Genesis 19. He reaches Zoar at sunrise, then leaves for the mountain.
places.limits: The exact site is not sure.

places.name: Gerar
places.summary: Abraham stays in Gerar in Genesis 20, and Abimelech takes Sarah. Isaac stays here in Genesis 26, and herdsmen argue over his wells.
places.limits: Tell Haror is a proposed site. The marker is a rough guide.

places.name: Beer Lahai Roi / Negev
places.summary: The LORD’s angel finds Hagar by a spring in Genesis 16. The well is then called Beer Lahai Roi. Isaac later lives near it.
places.limits: Its site is unknown. The marker shows only the Negev region.

places.name: Land of Moriah
places.summary: God sends Abraham to the land of Moriah to offer Isaac (Genesis 22). The LORD’s angel stops him there, and Abraham offers a ram.
places.limits: A later Bible book links Moriah with Jerusalem. Genesis gives no sure site.

places.name: Salem
places.summary: Melchizedek, king of Salem, meets Abram in Genesis 14. He is priest of God Most High.
places.limits: Tradition identifies Salem with Jerusalem. Genesis alone does not prove it.

places.name: Dan
places.summary: Abram chases the kings who took Lot as far as Dan (Genesis 14).
places.limits: The name Dan may come from a later time than Abram.

places.name: Damascus region
places.summary: Abram chases the kings to Hobah in Genesis 14. The text puts Hobah on the left hand of Damascus.
places.limits: The marker shows Damascus. Hobah’s exact site is unknown.

places.name: Gilead
places.summary: Laban catches up with Jacob in the mountain of Gilead (Genesis 31). They heap up stones and make a covenant there.
places.limits: The marker shows a hill region, not one spot.

places.name: Mahanaim
places.summary: God’s angels meet Jacob here in Genesis 32. Jacob says, “This is God’s army,” and names the place Mahanaim.
places.limits: The site is not sure. The marker shows the wider region.

places.name: Penuel / Jabbok
places.summary: Jacob wrestles a man until dawn near the ford of the Jabbok (Genesis 32). He names the place Peniel. He then meets Esau in Genesis 33.
places.limits: The marker follows a proposed site near the river.

places.name: Succoth
places.summary: Jacob builds a house and shelters for his livestock here in Genesis 33.
places.limits: The marker follows a proposed Jordan valley site.

places.name: Bethlehem / Ephrath
places.summary: Rachel dies giving birth to Benjamin on the way to Ephrath (Genesis 35). The text says Ephrath is also called Bethlehem.
places.limits: The marker shows the town. Traditions differ about where Rachel is buried.

places.name: Edom / Seir
places.summary: Esau lives in the hill country of Seir in Genesis 36. The chapter lists his sons and the chiefs of Edom.
places.limits: The marker shows a region, not a border.

places.name: Dothan
places.summary: Joseph finds his brothers at Dothan in Genesis 37. They throw him into a pit and sell him.
places.limits: Tell Dothan is the usual identification.

places.name: Adullam
places.summary: Judah visits Hirah, an Adullamite, in Genesis 38. Hirah later goes with Judah to Timnah.
places.limits: The marker follows the usual hill-country identification.

places.name: Timnah region
places.summary: Judah goes up to Timnah to shear his sheep in Genesis 38. Tamar waits for him on the road there.
places.limits: More than one ancient site has this name. The right one is not sure.

places.name: Canaan
places.summary: Jacob lives in Canaan during the famine. His sons travel from Canaan to Egypt for grain in Genesis 42–43. In Genesis 45 Joseph sends them back to bring Jacob.
places.limits: The marker shows a region, not a border.

sources.title: Book of Genesis · Wikipedia

contextGuide.title: Genesis: context and evidence
contextGuide.description: Explore the book’s larger concerns through selected passages and relevant evidence.

steps.title: Creation gives people a shared worth
steps.text: Six times the chapter says God saw that his work was good. People come last, and verse 31 says “very good.” Verse 27 says “image” twice and then names both male and female. No one group holds that standing alone. The command to rule in verse 28 comes after the blessing. Verses 29–30 then give plants as food to people and animals alike. So ruling here sits beside care for life that God called good.

steps.title: A grave becomes a claim to land
steps.text: God promised Abraham this land in 12:7 and 13:15. Yet in verse 4 he owns none of it and calls himself a foreigner. He is offered a free tomb twice and refuses both times. He wants a purchase made before witnesses (verses 13 and 16). Verses 17–18 read like a deed: field, cave, trees, borders, and witnesses. A grave is the first piece of the promised land he owns. A cuneiform tablet shows how another people recorded a field sale.

steps.title: Food storage creates political power
steps.text: Pharaoh asked for a meaning, and Joseph adds a plan (verses 33–36). The plan is practical: overseers, a fifth of each harvest, and stores in the cities. Verse 36 states its purpose: “that the land will not perish.” The stored grain is held “under the hand of Pharaoh” (verse 35). So saving lives and growing the king’s power arrive together. Chapter 47 shows what that power later costs the people. An Egyptian granary model shows scribes recording grain, as a comparison only.
